**Question.** Are there condition-specific eQTLs, i.e. genetic variants whose effect on gene
expression differs between conditions, and which eQTLs are shared?

**Method: mashr** (multivariate adaptive shrinkage; Urbut et al. 2019, *Nature Genetics*). mashr
takes the effect size (beta) and its standard error (SE) of the same gene-variant pairs in all
conditions at once, from each condition's FaST-LMM GWAS (`SnpWeight`, `SnpWeightSE` in the
`first_assoc` files). It

1. learns from the data which sharing patterns are common (e.g. "same effect everywhere",
   "only in fluconazole", "only in galactose") and how correlated the noise is between conditions
   (many strains were profiled in several conditions);
2. re-estimates every effect using these patterns (shrinkage). Noisy estimates from ~55-80 strains
   are pulled towards the pattern they fit best, which corrects the winner's curse (effects
   overestimated in the condition where the eQTL was found);
3. reports, for every eQTL and condition, the **lfsr** (local false sign rate: the probability that
   the sign of the effect is wrong; lfsr < 0.05 = confidently non-zero, like an FDR), and the
   posterior effect size.

mashr works on GWAS summary statistics, so conditions may have different strains and numbers of
strains: fewer strains give larger SEs and more shrinkage. It does not need the strains to be shared.

**Two sets of gene-variant pairs** (the same pairs in every condition, any p-value):

- *Strong set*: one lead variant per gene (lowest p-value) among the eQTLs significant in **at
  least one** condition of the run. Results are reported for these.
- *Random set*: a random sample of all tested gene-variant pairs (mostly no effect). Used to learn
  the noise correlation between conditions and the weights of the sharing patterns without the
  bias of selecting large effects.

**Runs.** Fluconazole_16ug and fluconazole_8ug are two drug doses, not replicates, and are
separate conditions. Integrated datasets are left out (they reuse the replicates' cells).

| Run | Conditions |
|---|---|
| A (main) | YPD.1, YPD.2, fluconazole_16ug, fluconazole_8ug, synthetic complete (sc2glu.2), galactose |

**Update 2026-10-27:** run C (YPD + fluconazole only, robustness check) is commented out and not
reported in the paper; its code is kept below as comments. Its cached fit
(`../results/mashr/mash_C_YPD_flu.rds`) and earlier outputs are left on disk but no longer used.

**Definitions used for the results** (following Urbut et al. 2019):

- *Significant in a condition*: lfsr < 0.05.
- *Shared by sign*: significant in at least one of two conditions and same sign of the posterior
  effect in both.
- *Shared by magnitude*: same sign and posterior effects within a factor of 2 of each other.
- *Condition-specific (by magnitude)*: significant in that condition, and its posterior effect is
  **not** shared by magnitude with any other condition of the run (in every other condition it is
  less than half as large, more than twice as large, or of opposite sign).
- *Significant in only one condition*: lfsr < 0.05 in that condition and >= 0.05 in all others
  (a stricter, power-dependent definition, shown for comparison).
- *Fluconazole-specific*: significant in a fluconazole dose and not shared by magnitude with
  either YPD replicate.

The YPD.1 vs YPD.2 pair is the built-in reference: replicates of the same condition should share
almost every eQTL, so sharing between different conditions is read against it.

# 1. Datasets and inputs

```{r config}
ROOT <- "/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all"
OUTPUT_DIR <- "../results/mashr"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
N_CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "16"))
set.seed(42)

SNP_DIR   <- "results_SNPs_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
INDEL_DIR <- "results_Indels_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
CNV_DIR   <- "results_CNVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17"   # CNV GWAS re-run without chr17
SV_DIR    <- "results_SVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files"
VARIANTS  <- c("SNPs", "InDels", "SVs", "CNVs")

make_cond <- function(res, tag, indel_dir = INDEL_DIR,
                      indel_file = paste0("all_signif_Indels_", tag, "_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")) {
  res <- file.path(ROOT, res)
  list(signif = c(
         SNPs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SNPs_", tag, "_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")),
         InDels = file.path(res, indel_file),
         SVs    = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SVs_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_with_threshold.txt")),
         CNVs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_CNV_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17_with_threshold.txt"))),
       dirs = c(SNPs = file.path(res, SNP_DIR), InDels = file.path(res, indel_dir),
                SVs = file.path(res, SV_DIR), CNVs = file.path(res, CNV_DIR)))
}

CONDS <- list(
  YPD.1     = make_cond("YPD.1/fastlmm/results", "YPD.1",   # YPD.1's InDel run: other folder, same indels.96samples

missing <- c(unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "signif")), unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "dirs")))
```

# 2. Strong and random sets

```{r sets}
# strong set: lead variant (lowest p) per gene among eQTLs significant in >= 1 condition of the run
lead_per_gene <- function(conds) bind_rows(signif[conds]) %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>% slice_min(P, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type)
strong <- lapply(RUNS, lead_per_gene)

# random set: per variant type, random genes and random variants from YPD.1's full GWAS output
N_RANDOM_GENES <- 1000; N_VAR_PER_GENE <- 5
RANDOM_SEED <- 42
random_cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "random_pairs.rds")
if (file.exists(random_cache)) {
  random_pairs <- readRDS(random_cache)
} else {
  # Reproducible draw: genes are sorted before sampling and every draw has its own fixed seed, so
  # the same pairs are drawn whatever the earlier random calls, file-listing order or number of
  # parallel workers (forked workers do not share the parent's random-number stream).
  # The pairs used in the paper (drawn 2026-10-26 with the earlier code) are in random_pairs.rds;
  # this code only runs if that file is missing, and would then draw a different, reproducible set.
  random_pairs <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(VARIANTS), function(v) {
    vt <- VARIANTS[v]; d <- CONDS$YPD.1$dirs[[vt]]
    genes <- sort(list.dirs(d, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE))
    set.seed(RANDOM_SEED + v)
    genes <- sample(genes, min(N_RANDOM_GENES, length(genes)))
    bind_rows(mclapply(seq_along(genes), function(i) {
      g <- genes[i]
      f <- file.path(d, g, paste0(g, ".first_assoc.txt"))
      if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
      snps <- tryCatch(sort(fread(f, select = "SNP", showProgress = FALSE)$SNP), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!length(snps)) return(NULL)
      set.seed(RANDOM_SEED + 1e5 * v + i)
      tibble(Gene = g, SNP = sample(snps, min(N_VAR_PER_GENE, length(snps))), Variant_Type = vt)
    }, mc.cores = N_CORES))
  }))
  saveRDS(random_pairs, random_cache)
}

knitr::kable(tibble(set = c(paste("strong,", RUN_LABELS[names(strong)]), "random"),
                    gene_variant_pairs = c(sapply(strong, nrow), nrow(random_pairs))))
```

# 3. Extract beta and SE in every condition

For every pair of the strong sets and the random set, the effect size and SE are read from each
condition's full GWAS output (`first_assoc` files), whatever the p-value. Cached per condition
to `extract_<condition>.rds`.

```{r extract}
all_pairs <- bind_rows(c(strong, list(random_pairs))) %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type)

extract_condition <- function(cn) {
  cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("extract_", cn, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache)) return(readRDS(cache))
  jobs <- all_pairs %>% group_by(Variant_Type, Gene) %>% summarise(snps = list(SNP), .groups = "drop")
  res <- mclapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
    vt <- jobs$Variant_Type[i]; g <- jobs$Gene[i]
    f <- file.path(CONDS[[cn]]$dirs[[vt]], g, paste0(g, ".first_assoc.txt"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
    d <- tryCatch(fread(f, select = c("SNP", "SnpWeight", "SnpWeightSE", "PValue"), showProgress = FALSE),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
    d <- d[SNP %in% jobs$snps[[i]]]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    d[, `:=`(Gene = g, Variant_Type = vt)]
  }, mc.cores = N_CORES)
  ex <- rbindlist(res) %>% as.data.frame() %>% distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE)
  saveRDS(ex, cache)
  ex
}
extracted <- lapply(setNames(names(CONDS), names(CONDS)), extract_condition)
knitr::kable(tibble(condition = LABELS[names(extracted)], pairs_found = sapply(extracted, nrow),
                    of_total = nrow(all_pairs)))
```

# 4. Fit mashr

Steps, following the mashr eQTL vignette:

1. Noise correlation between conditions (`estimate_null_correlation_simple`) from the random set.
2. Data-driven sharing patterns from the strong set: principal components (`cov_pca`) refined by
   extreme deconvolution (`cov_ed`), plus the canonical patterns (`cov_canonical`: no sharing,
   condition-specific for each condition, equal effects, simple correlations).
3. Fit the mixture weights of these patterns on the random set (`mash`).
4. Apply the fitted model to the strong set (`fixg = TRUE`) to get posterior effects and lfsr.

Missing values (gene-variant pair not tested in a condition) are set to beta = 0 and SE = 1000
in the strong set, so they carry no information; random-set pairs with any missing value are dropped.

```{r fit}
make_mats <- function(pairs, conds) {
  key <- paste(pairs$Gene, pairs$SNP, pairs$Variant_Type, sep = "|")
  B <- S <- matrix(NA_real_, length(key), length(conds), dimnames = list(key, conds))
  for (cn in conds) {
    e <- extracted[[cn]]
    m <- match(key, paste(e$Gene, e$SNP, e$Variant_Type, sep = "|"))
    B[, cn] <- e$SnpWeight[m]; S[, cn] <- e$SnpWeightSE[m]
  }
  bad <- is.na(B) | is.na(S) | !is.finite(S) | S <= 0
  list(B = B, S = S, bad = bad)
}

fit_run <- function(run) {
  cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("mash_", run, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache)) return(readRDS(cache))
  conds <- RUNS[[run]]
  ms <- make_mats(strong[[run]], conds)
  n_missing_strong <- sum(rowSums(ms$bad) > 0)
  ms$B[ms$bad] <- 0; ms$S[ms$bad] <- 1e3
  mr <- make_mats(random_pairs, conds)
  keep <- rowSums(mr$bad) == 0
  mr$B <- mr$B[keep, , drop = FALSE]; mr$S <- mr$S[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  d_tmp    <- mash_set_data(mr$B, mr$S)
  Vhat     <- estimate_null_correlation_simple(d_tmp)
  d_random <- mash_set_data(mr$B, mr$S, V = Vhat)
  d_strong <- mash_set_data(ms$B, ms$S, V = Vhat)
  U_pca <- cov_pca(d_strong, npc = min(5, length(conds) - 1))
  U_ed  <- cov_ed(d_strong, U_pca)
  U_c   <- cov_canonical(d_random)
  m_random <- mash(d_random, Ulist = c(U_ed, U_c), outputlevel = 1)
  m_strong <- mash(d_strong, g = get_fitted_g(m_random), fixg = TRUE)
  out <- list(conds = conds, Vhat = Vhat, m_random = m_random, m_strong = m_strong,
              n_strong = nrow(ms$B), n_missing_strong = n_missing_strong, n_random = nrow(mr$B))
  saveRDS(out, cache)
  out
}
fits <- lapply(setNames(names(RUNS), names(RUNS)), fit_run)

# Strong-set eQTLs whose lead variant has no local / distant call are dropped from every result
# below. These are CNVs of non-S288C ("YX") genes placed past an S288C chromosome end: they have no
# reference position, and the same CNVs are left out of the variant counts (Supplementary Table 1).
# With the pattern weights fixed (fitted on the random set), mashr computes each strong-set eQTL's
# posterior on its own, so dropping rows after fitting gives the same results for the other eQTLs.
ANNOT_DIRS <- c(YPD.1 = "Figure.3/Fig.3-Panel-A-C-D-cis-and-trans-eqtl-YPD-variant-type/results/YPD.1/annotations",
                YPD.2 = "Figure.4/Fig.4-YPD.2/results/YPD.2/annotations",
                Flu_16ug = "Figure.4/Fig.4-Flu.1/results/Flu.1/annotations",
                Flu_8ug = "Figure.4/Fig.4-Flu.2/results/Flu.2/annotations",
                sc2glu.2 = "Figure.4/Fig.4-sc2glu.2_only/results/sc2glu.2_only/annotations",
                galactose = "Figure.4/Fig.4-scgal.1/results/scgal.1/annotations")
ANNOT_FILES <- c(SNPs = "snp", InDels = "indel", SVs = "sv", CNVs = "cnv")
annot <- bind_rows(lapply(names(ANNOT_DIRS), function(cn) bind_rows(imap(ANNOT_FILES, function(f, vt)
  fread(file.path(ROOT, "Agrawal_single_cell_eqtl_cell_cycle", ANNOT_DIRS[[cn]], paste0(f, "_data_annotated_cis_trans.txt")),
        sep = "\t", quote = "", select = c("Pheno", "SNP", "clump_members", "local_distant"), data.table = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Variant_Type = vt, dataset = cn)))))

# every clump member gets its clump's call
ld_calls <- annot %>%
  mutate(member = strsplit(coalesce(clump_members, SNP), ";")) %>% unnest(member) %>%
  distinct(Gene = Pheno, SNP = member, Variant_Type, local_distant)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(ld_calls %>% select(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type))))   # one call per gene-variant pair
keep_called <- function(m) {
  k <- rownames(m$result$PosteriorMean)
  ok <- paste(k) %in% paste(ld_calls$Gene, ld_calls$SNP, ld_calls$Variant_Type, sep = "|")
  for (nm in names(m$result)) if (is.matrix(m$result[[nm]])) m$result[[nm]] <- m$result[[nm]][ok, , drop = FALSE]
  attr(m, "n_dropped") <- sum(!ok)
  m
}
for (r in names(fits)) {
  fits[[r]]$m_strong <- keep_called(fits[[r]]$m_strong)
  fits[[r]]$n_dropped_no_call <- attr(fits[[r]]$m_strong, "n_dropped")
  fits[[r]]$n_strong <- nrow(fits[[r]]$m_strong$result$PosteriorMean)
}
knitr::kable(tibble(run = RUN_LABELS[names(fits)],
                    strong_eQTLs = sapply(fits, `[[`, "n_strong"),
                    dropped_no_local_distant_call = sapply(fits, `[[`, "n_dropped_no_call"),
                    strong_with_a_missing_condition = sapply(fits, `[[`, "n_missing_strong"),
                    random_pairs_used = sapply(fits, `[[`, "n_random"),
                    log_likelihood_random = sapply(fits, function(f) get_loglik(f$m_random))),
             caption = "mashr fits")
```

# 5. Results per run

```{r results-functions}
lab <- function(x) unname(LABELS[x])

# condition-specific calls from posterior means and lfsr
specific_calls <- function(f) {
  pm <- get_pm(f$m_strong); lf <- get_lfsr(f$m_strong); conds <- f$conds
  sig <- lf < 0.05
  shared_mag <- function(a, b) sign(a) == sign(b) & abs(a / b) >= 0.5 & abs(a / b) <= 2
  out <- lapply(conds, function(cn) {
    others <- setdiff(conds, cn)
    not_shared <- sapply(others, function(o) !shared_mag(pm[, o], pm[, cn]))
    tibble(eQTL = rownames(pm), condition = cn, significant = sig[, cn],
           specific_by_magnitude = sig[, cn] & apply(not_shared, 1, all),
           significant_only_here = sig[, cn] & rowSums(sig[, others, drop = FALSE]) == 0)
  })
  bind_rows(out)
}

flu_specific <- function(f) {
  pm <- get_pm(f$m_strong); lf <- get_lfsr(f$m_strong)
  shared_mag <- function(a, b) sign(a) == sign(b) & abs(a / b) >= 0.5 & abs(a / b) <= 2
  dose_spec <- function(d) lf[, d] < 0.05 & !shared_mag(pm[, "YPD.1"], pm[, d]) & !shared_mag(pm[, "YPD.2"], pm[, d])
  tibble(eQTL = rownames(pm),
         fluconazole_16ug_specific = dose_spec("Flu_16ug"),
         fluconazole_8ug_specific  = dose_spec("Flu_8ug"),
         both_doses_specific = dose_spec("Flu_16ug") & dose_spec("Flu_8ug")) %>%
    separate(eQTL, c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE)
}

sharing_heatmap <- function(mat, title) {
  d <- as.data.frame(as.table(mat)) %>% setNames(c("c1", "c2", "share")) %>%
    mutate(c1 = factor(lab(as.character(c1)), lab(rownames(mat))), c2 = factor(lab(as.character(c2)), rev(lab(rownames(mat)))))
  ggplot(d, aes(c1, c2, fill = share)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", share)), size = 3.4) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2C7FB8", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Proportion\nshared") +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
}
```

```{r results, results = "asis", fig.width = 15, fig.height = 6.5}
summary_rows <- list(); flu_sets <- list()
for (run in names(fits)) {
  f <- fits[[run]]; conds <- f$conds
  cat("\n\n## ", RUN_LABELS[[run]], "\n\n", sep = "")

  # mixture weights: which sharing patterns does the data support?
  pi_hat <- get_estimated_pi(f$m_random)
  cat("\n**Weights of the sharing patterns** (fitted on the random set; `null` = no effect).\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(tibble(pattern = names(pi_hat), weight = round(pi_hat, 4)) %>% arrange(desc(weight)) %>% head(12)))

  # how many conditions is each eQTL significant in?
  lf <- get_lfsr(f$m_strong)
  n_sig <- rowSums(lf < 0.05)
  cat("\n\n**Number of conditions in which each eQTL is significant (lfsr < 0.05)**\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(n_conditions_significant = n_sig))))

  # per-condition counts
  calls <- specific_calls(f)
  per_cond <- calls %>% group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(significant = sum(significant), specific_by_magnitude = sum(specific_by_magnitude),
              significant_only_here = sum(significant_only_here), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct_specific_by_magnitude = 100 * specific_by_magnitude / significant,
           condition = factor(condition, conds)) %>% arrange(condition) %>%
    mutate(condition = lab(as.character(condition)))
  cat("\n\n**Per condition** (strong-set eQTLs)\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(per_cond, digits = 1))
  summary_rows[[run]] <- per_cond %>% mutate(run = RUN_LABELS[[run]])

  # fluconazole-specific eQTLs
  fs <- flu_specific(f)
  flu_sets[[run]] <- fs
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**Fluconazole-specific eQTLs** (significant in the dose, not shared by magnitude with YPD.1 or YPD.2): fluconazole_16ug %d, fluconazole_8ug %d, both doses %d.\n\n",
              sum(fs$fluconazole_16ug_specific), sum(fs$fluconazole_8ug_specific), sum(fs$both_doses_specific)))

  # pairwise sharing
  sh_mag  <- get_pairwise_sharing(f$m_strong, factor = 0.5)
  sh_sign <- get_pairwise_sharing(f$m_strong, factor = 0)
  write.csv(sh_mag,  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("pairwise_sharing_magnitude_", run, ".csv")))
  write.csv(sh_sign, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("pairwise_sharing_sign_", run, ".csv")))
  p <- sharing_heatmap(sh_sign, "Shared by sign") + sharing_heatmap(sh_mag, "Shared by magnitude (within 2-fold)") +
    plot_annotation(title = RUN_LABELS[[run]], theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)))
  print(p)
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_pairwise_sharing_", run, ".tiff")), p, width = 15, height = 6.5,
         dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")

  # per-eQTL table
  pm <- get_pm(f$m_strong); psd <- get_psd(f$m_strong)
  colnames(pm)  <- paste0("posterior_beta_", colnames(pm))
  colnames(lf)  <- paste0("lfsr_", colnames(lf))
  colnames(psd) <- paste0("posterior_sd_", colnames(psd))
  tab <- tibble(eQTL = rownames(pm)) %>% separate(eQTL, c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE) %>%
    bind_cols(as_tibble(pm), as_tibble(psd), as_tibble(lf)) %>%
    mutate(n_conditions_significant = n_sig) %>%
    left_join(calls %>% filter(specific_by_magnitude) %>% group_by(eQTL) %>%
                summarise(specific_to = paste(lab(condition), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop"), by = "eQTL") %>%
    left_join(fs %>% select(eQTL, fluconazole_16ug_specific, fluconazole_8ug_specific, both_doses_specific), by = "eQTL")
  write.csv(tab, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("mash_results_", run, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# 7. Dataset quality: cells and sequencing depth per dataset

Expression of each strain is a pseudobulk (sum over its cells). Its precision depends on the number
of cells per strain and the reads (UMIs) per cell. Because expression is rank-normalised (INT) per
condition, a noisier dataset gives *smaller* standardised effect sizes even if the true genetic
effect is the same: measurement noise adds non-genetic variance. Numbers are from the filtered
single-cell objects used for the pseudobulks (`Na_va_data_subsetted.rds`).

```{r dataset-qc}
QC_DIRS <- c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1", YPD.2 = "YPD.2", Flu_16ug = "Flu.1", Flu_8ug = "Flu.2", sc2glu.2 = "sc2glu.2", galactose = "scgal.1")
qc_cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "dataset_qc.rds")
if (file.exists(qc_cache)) {
  qc <- readRDS(qc_cache)
} else {
  qc <- bind_rows(lapply(names(QC_DIRS), function(k) {
    o <- readRDS(file.path(ROOT, QC_DIRS[[k]], "gene_expression_analysis/output_from_pseudobulk_fastlmm/Na_va_data_subsetted.rds"))
    m <- o@meta.data; rm(o); gc()
    ps <- m %>% group_by(strain = SNG.BEST.GUESS) %>% summarise(cells = n(), umi = sum(nCount_RNA), .groups = "drop")
    tibble(dataset = k, cells = nrow(m), strains = nrow(ps), median_cells_per_strain = median(ps$cells),
           strains_with_lt20_cells = sum(ps$cells < 20), median_UMI_per_cell = median(m$nCount_RNA),
           median_genes_per_cell = median(m$nFeature_RNA), median_UMI_per_strain = median(ps$umi))
  }))
  saveRDS(qc, qc_cache)
}
fA <- fits$A_main
eff <- apply(abs(get_pm(fA$m_strong)), 2, median)
qc <- qc %>% mutate(median_abs_posterior_beta_runA = eff[dataset], condition = lab(dataset)) %>%
  relocate(condition) %>% select(-dataset) %>% arrange(desc(median_UMI_per_strain))
write.csv(qc, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "dataset_qc.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(qc, digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Cells, depth and median effect size per dataset (sorted by UMIs per strain)")
```

Effect sizes follow sequencing depth: the deepest datasets (YPD.1, YPD.2) have the largest
standardised effects and the shallowest (fluconazole_16ug, galactose) the smallest. Weaker effects in
a condition can therefore reflect less precise expression measurement rather than biology.

# 8. Condition-specific eQTLs defined with replicates

Single-dataset calls (Section 5) are dominated by dataset-specific signals (e.g. YPD.2). Here a
condition-specific eQTL must be supported by all datasets of that condition:

- *YPD-specific*: significant (lfsr < 0.05) in **both** YPD replicates and not shared by magnitude
  (same sign, within 2-fold) with any other condition.
- *Fluconazole-specific*: significant at **both** doses and not shared by magnitude with any other
  condition (YPD replicates, synthetic complete, galactose). In run A this is the same set of genes
  as "not shared with either YPD replicate" (checked 2026-10-28), so only one call is shown.
- *Galactose- / synthetic-complete-specific*: significant in that dataset and not shared by
  magnitude with any other. Each condition has one dataset, so these calls are not confirmed by a
  replicate.
- *Replicate noise*: the same rule applied between the two YPD replicates (significant in one, not
  shared with the other): the number of "specific" calls expected without any change of condition.

```{r replicate-consistent}
rep_calls <- function(run) {
  f <- fits[[run]]; pm <- get_pm(f$m_strong); lf <- get_lfsr(f$m_strong); conds <- f$conds
  sg <- function(c) lf[, c] < 0.05
  sh <- function(a, b) sign(pm[, a]) == sign(pm[, b]) & abs(pm[, b] / pm[, a]) >= 0.5 & abs(pm[, b] / pm[, a]) <= 2
  nonY <- setdiff(conds, c("YPD.1", "YPD.2")); nonF <- setdiff(conds, c("Flu_16ug", "Flu_8ug"))
  out <- list(
    "YPD-specific (both YPD replicates)" = sg("YPD.1") & sg("YPD.2") & Reduce(`&`, lapply(nonY, function(o) !sh("YPD.1", o) & !sh("YPD.2", o))),
    # not shared with any other condition; same 9 genes as "not shared with either YPD replicate" in run A
    "Fluconazole-specific (both doses)" =
      sg("Flu_16ug") & sg("Flu_8ug") & Reduce(`&`, lapply(nonF, function(o) !sh("Flu_16ug", o) & !sh("Flu_8ug", o))),
    "Galactose-specific" = if ("galactose" %in% conds)
      sg("galactose") & Reduce(`&`, lapply(setdiff(conds, "galactose"), function(o) !sh("galactose", o))) else NULL,
    "Synthetic-complete-specific" = if ("sc2glu.2" %in% conds)
      sg("sc2glu.2") & Reduce(`&`, lapply(setdiff(conds, "sc2glu.2"), function(o) !sh("sc2glu.2", o))) else NULL,
    "Replicate noise: significant in YPD.1, not shared with YPD.2" = sg("YPD.1") & !sh("YPD.1", "YPD.2"),
    "Replicate noise: significant in YPD.2, not shared with YPD.1" = sg("YPD.2") & !sh("YPD.2", "YPD.1"))
  out <- Filter(Negate(is.null), out)
  tibble(call = names(out), n = sapply(out, sum), run = RUN_LABELS[[run]])
}
rc <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), rep_calls)) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = n)
# y-axis labels of the figures (9.6, 9.6b): the legend says "Condition-specific", so drop "-specific"
call_axis_label <- function(x) recode(x,
  "YPD-specific (both YPD replicates)" = "YPD (both replicates)",
  "Fluconazole-specific (both doses)"  = "Fluconazole (both doses)",
  "Galactose-specific"                 = "Synthetic complete with galactose",
  "Synthetic-complete-specific"        = "Synthetic complete with glucose")
write.csv(rc, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "replicate_consistent_condition_specific_calls.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(rc, caption = "Condition-specific eQTLs (genes) defined with replicates, vs replicate noise")
```

# 9. Figures

Figures modelled on Urbut et al. (2019), Figs. 2-4. Run A (six conditions) unless stated. All are
saved to `results/mashr/` as TIFF (600 dpi) and PNG.

```{r fig-setup}
COND_COLS <- c("YPD.1" = "#81C784", "YPD.2" = "#2E7D32", "fluconazole_16ug" = "#BA68C8",
               "fluconazole_8ug" = "#6A1B9A", "synthetic complete with glucose" = "#E53935", "synthetic complete with galactose" = "#F9C80E")
save_fig <- function(p, name, w, h) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".tiff")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".png")),  p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
}
fA <- fits$A_main
condsA <- fA$conds
piA <- get_estimated_pi(fA$m_random)
UA  <- fA$m_random$fitted_g$Ulist
```

## 9.1 Weights of the sharing patterns

How common each pattern is among all gene-variant pairs (fitted on the random set). `null` = no
effect; `ED_*` = patterns learned from the data; `equal_effects` = the same effect in every
condition; a condition name = an effect in that condition only.

```{r fig-weights, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5}
w <- tibble(pattern = names(piA), weight = piA) %>%
  filter(weight > 0) %>%
  mutate(kind = case_when(pattern == "null" ~ "No effect",
                          grepl("^ED_", pattern) ~ "Data-driven pattern of sharing",
                          # only equal_effects of these canonical patterns has a non-zero weight in run A
                          pattern %in% c("equal_effects", "identity") | grepl("^simple_het", pattern) ~ "Equal effects",
                          TRUE ~ "One dataset only"),
         label = ifelse(pattern %in% condsA, paste0(lab(pattern), " only"), pattern),
         label = fct_reorder(label, weight))
p <- ggplot(w, aes(weight * 100, label, fill = kind)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%%", weight * 100)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No effect" = "grey75", "Data-driven pattern of sharing" = "#2C7FB8",
                               "Equal effects" = "#41AB5D", "One dataset only" = "#E6550D"), name = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(title = "Estimated weights of the sharing patterns (run A)", x = "Weight (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "bottom",
                                        axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_pattern_weights", 9, 5.5)
```

## 9.2 The main learned sharing patterns

(a) Correlation matrix of the most heavily weighted learned pattern (`ED_PCA_1`). (b-d) Leading
eigenvector (direction of effects across conditions) of each of the three most heavily weighted
learned patterns. Each learned pattern is dominated by one direction (its first eigenvector
explains >80% of its variance; the other eigenvalues are equal and their eigenvectors therefore
arbitrary), so each pattern is summarised by its leading direction:

- (b) the main pattern: effects of the same sign in all conditions (broad sharing);
- (c, d) the next patterns: contrasts between conditions, i.e. effects stronger in some conditions
  than in others. Their weights (in the titles) show how rarely they occur.

```{r fig-patterns, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 9}
# patterns drawn: ED_PCA_1 and ED_PCA_2 (the two leading patterns learned from the strong set, drawn
# whatever their weight: ED_PCA_2, the YPD vs synthetic-media contrast, has weight 0 in the seeded
# fit and in all five random sets of mashr_seed_robustness.R), then any other data-driven pattern
# with a non-zero weight, up to three in total
# patterns drawn: data-driven patterns with weight >= 0.01% (only ED_PCA_1 in the seeded fit;
# ED_PCA_2, the YPD vs synthetic-media contrast, has weight 0 in all five random sets of
# mashr_seed_robustness.R, and ED_PCA_5 has 0.004%)
ed <- names(sort(piA[grepl("^ED_", names(piA)) & piA >= 1e-4], decreasing = TRUE))
ed <- head(ed, 3)
cm <- cov2cor(UA[[ed[1]]]); dimnames(cm) <- list(lab(condsA), lab(condsA))
heat <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm)) %>% setNames(c("c1", "c2", "r")) %>%
  mutate(c1 = factor(c1, lab(condsA)), c2 = factor(c2, rev(lab(condsA))))
pa <- ggplot(heat, aes(c1, c2, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +
  labs(title = sprintf("(a) Correlation of effects, %s (weight %.1f%%)", ed[1], 100 * piA[ed[1]]), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, colour = "black"),
                                        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
eig_bar <- function(nm, letter) {
  e <- eigen(UA[[nm]]); v <- e$vectors[, 1]; if (sum(v) < 0) v <- -v
  d <- tibble(condition = factor(lab(condsA), lab(condsA)), loading = v)
  ggplot(d, aes(condition, loading, fill = condition)) + geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + scale_fill_manual(values = COND_COLS, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = sprintf("(%s) %s: leading eigenvector", letter, nm),
         subtitle = sprintf("pattern weight %.2f%%; %.0f%% of the pattern's variance", 100 * piA[nm], 100 * e$values[1] / sum(e$values)),
         x = NULL, y = "Loading") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, colour = "black"),
                                          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey30"))
}
# free(): panel (c) sits under the heatmap; without it its y-axis title is aligned with the heatmap's
# long condition labels and ends up far from the axis
eig_rest <- lapply(seq_along(ed)[-1], function(i) eig_bar(ed[i], letters[i + 1]))
p <- (pa | eig_bar(ed[1], "b"))
if (length(eig_rest)) p <- p / wrap_plots(eig_rest, nrow = 1)
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_learned_patterns", 15, 9)
```

### 9.2b Correlation matrix of the data-driven pattern with the largest mash weight

As in Urbut et al. (2019), Fig. 2a: the covariance matrix with the largest mash weight
(`ED_PCA_1`), shown as correlations between conditions. Same matrix as panel (a) above, as a
single figure.

```{r fig-top-matrix-heatmap, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 6}
top_ed <- names(which.max(piA[grepl("^ED_", names(piA))]))
cm_top <- cov2cor(UA[[top_ed]]); dimnames(cm_top) <- list(lab(condsA), lab(condsA))
heat_top <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm_top)) %>% setNames(c("c1", "c2", "r")) %>%
  mutate(c1 = factor(c1, lab(condsA)), c2 = factor(c2, rev(lab(condsA))))
p <- ggplot(heat_top, aes(c1, c2, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Correlation of effects, %s (mash weight %.1f%%)", top_ed, 100 * piA[[top_ed]]), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, colour = "black"),
                                        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
                                        panel.grid = element_blank())
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_top_matrix_correlation_heatmap", 7.5, 6)
```

### 9.2c Publication panels (one file per panel)

The panels of 9.2 as separate figures in the style of the Figure 3 panels
(`Figure.3/Fig.3-Panel-A-C-D-cis-and-trans-eqtl-YPD-variant-type/codes/Fig3_panel_B_C_D_variant_eqtl_classification.Rmd`:
`theme_classic`, default font, bold black axis text and titles at 18 pt, black bar outlines, bold
in-plot labels, x labels at 45 degrees). Dataset names are the same in every panel (`PUB_LAB`).
Files `Fig_mash_pub_*` in `results/mashr/`:

- `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_1_heatmap`: correlations of the pattern with the largest mash weight (main figure)
- `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_1_eigenvector`, `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_2_eigenvector`,
  `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_4_eigenvector`: leading eigenvector of each pattern

All panels are saved at the same size (8.5 x 8 in) so they can be arranged on one sheet with the
same text size. Titles give the pattern and its mash weight only; the share of each pattern's
variance carried by its leading eigenvector is in the table below (for the legend).
- `Fig_mash_pub_supp_ED_PCA_2_ED_PCA_4_heatmaps`: supplementary figure, correlation heatmaps of the
  next two data-driven patterns (also saved separately as `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_2_heatmap` and
  `Fig_mash_pub_ED_PCA_4_heatmap`)

```{r fig-patterns-pub}
# ── Publication theme: same as Figure 3 (Fig3_panel_B_C_D_variant_eqtl_classification.Rmd) ──
PUB_FONT  <- ""                 # default font, as in Figure 3
AXIS_SIZE <- 18                 # axis text and titles, bold (Figure 3 AXIS_SIZE)
PUB_SMALL <- 16                 # legend entries
PUB_LABEL <- 5.5                # in-plot labels, bold, mm (Figure 3 NLAB_SIZE)

pub_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = AXIS_SIZE, color = "black"),
    axis.text    = element_text(face = "bold", size = AXIS_SIZE, color = "black"),
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = AXIS_SIZE),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = PUB_SMALL),
    legend.text  = element_text(face = "bold", size = PUB_SMALL),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

# condition names for the paper (fluconazole doses named by ug/ml)
PUB_LAB <- c(YPD.1 = "YPD.1", YPD.2 = "YPD.2", Flu_16ug = "fluconazole.16", Flu_8ug = "fluconazole.8",
             sc2glu.2 = "synthetic complete with glucose", galactose = "synthetic complete with galactose")
PUB_COLS <- setNames(COND_COLS[lab(condsA)], PUB_LAB[condsA])

# Panels are saved separately but combined on one sheet: every panel gets the same canvas
# (PANEL_W x PANEL_H in) and the same title format, "<pattern> (weight x%)", so a pattern's heatmap
# and eigenvector match. The % of variance of the leading eigenvector is printed, not plotted
# (it belongs in the legend / methods).
PANEL_W <- 8.5; PANEL_H <- 8
pattern_title <- function(nm) {
  w <- 100 * piA[[nm]]
  sprintf("%s (weight %s%%)", nm, if (w >= 1) sprintf("%.1f", w) else if (w == 0) "0" else sprintf("%.2f", w))
}

pub_heatmap <- function(nm) {
  cm <- cov2cor(UA[[nm]]); dimnames(cm) <- list(PUB_LAB[condsA], PUB_LAB[condsA])
  d <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm)) %>% setNames(c("c1", "c2", "r")) %>%
    mutate(c1 = factor(c1, PUB_LAB[condsA]), c2 = factor(c2, rev(PUB_LAB[condsA])))
  ggplot(d, aes(c1, c2, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = PUB_LABEL - 0.5, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1),
                         breaks = c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), name = "Correlation") +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = pattern_title(nm), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    pub_theme +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

pub_eigen <- function(nm) {
  e <- eigen(UA[[nm]]); v <- e$vectors[, 1]; if (sum(v) < 0) v <- -v
  d <- tibble(condition = factor(PUB_LAB[condsA], PUB_LAB[condsA]), loading = v)
  ggplot(d, aes(condition, loading, fill = condition)) +
    geom_col(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PUB_COLS, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = pattern_title(nm), x = NULL, y = "Loading (leading eigenvector)") +
    pub_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

for (nm in ed) {
  p <- pub_heatmap(nm); print(p); save_fig(p, paste0("Fig_mash_pub_", nm, "_heatmap"), PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
  p <- pub_eigen(nm);   print(p); save_fig(p, paste0("Fig_mash_pub_", nm, "_eigenvector"), PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
}
# for the legend / methods: share of each pattern's variance carried by its leading eigenvector
knitr::kable(tibble(pattern = ed, weight_pct = round(100 * piA[ed], 3),
                    leading_eigenvector_pct_variance = sapply(ed, function(nm) {
                      ev <- eigen(UA[[nm]], only.values = TRUE)$values; round(100 * ev[1] / sum(ev), 1) })))

# supplementary figure: correlation heatmaps of the second and third data-driven patterns
if (length(ed) >= 2) {
  p <- wrap_plots(lapply(ed[-1], pub_heatmap), nrow = 1) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a", tag_prefix = "(", tag_suffix = ")") &
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = AXIS_SIZE, face = "bold"))
  print(p); save_fig(p, paste0("Fig_mash_pub_supp_", paste(ed[-1], collapse = "_"), "_heatmaps"), (length(ed) - 1) * PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
}
```

## 9.3 mash uses the learned sharing patterns to inform the effect estimates

For example eQTLs: each coloured dot is the original (raw) GWAS effect estimate in one condition,
with its 95% interval (±1.96 SE); the black dot is the mashr estimate (posterior mean, ±1.96
posterior SD). Noisy estimates are pulled towards the shared pattern; precise ones barely move.
Examples: the most significant eQTL overall, an eQTL with a noisy estimate in a low-depth
condition, and the strongest fluconazole-specific candidate.

```{r fig-shrinkage-examples, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 5.5}
pmA <- get_pm(fA$m_strong); psA <- get_psd(fA$m_strong); lfA <- get_lfsr(fA$m_strong)
raw_mat <- function(keys, what) sapply(condsA, function(cn) {
  e <- extracted[[cn]]; m <- match(keys, paste(e$Gene, e$SNP, e$Variant_Type, sep = "|")); e[[what]][m] })
keys <- rownames(pmA)
B <- raw_mat(keys, "SnpWeight"); S <- raw_mat(keys, "SnpWeightSE")
rownames(B) <- rownames(S) <- keys
# example 1: significant in the most conditions (all of them if any), largest effects
complete <- rowSums(is.na(B)) == 0   # examples must be tested in every condition
allsig <- which(complete & rowSums(lfA < 0.05) == max(rowSums(lfA[complete, , drop = FALSE] < 0.05)))
ex1 <- keys[allsig][which.max(rowSums(abs(pmA[allsig, , drop = FALSE])))]
noisy <- which(complete & rowSums(lfA < 0.05) >= max(2, max(rowSums(lfA < 0.05)) - 1))
ex2 <- keys[noisy][which.max(abs(B[noisy, "galactose"] - pmA[noisy, "galactose"]))]
fs <- flu_specific(fA)
f8 <- intersect(fs$eQTL[fs$fluconazole_8ug_specific], keys[complete])
ex3 <- if (length(f8)) f8[which.max(abs(pmA[f8, "Flu_8ug"]))] else keys[complete][1]
ex_plot <- function(k, title) {
  d <- tibble(condition = factor(lab(condsA), lab(condsA)), raw = B[k, ], raw_se = S[k, ], pm = pmA[k, ], psd = psA[k, ])
  ggplot(d, aes(y = condition)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = raw - 1.96 * raw_se, xmax = raw + 1.96 * raw_se, colour = condition), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8,
                   position = position_nudge(y = 0.15)) +
    geom_point(aes(raw, colour = condition), size = 3, position = position_nudge(y = 0.15)) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pm - 1.96 * psd, xmax = pm + 1.96 * psd), height = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8,
                   position = position_nudge(y = -0.15)) +
    geom_point(aes(pm), colour = "black", size = 2.5, position = position_nudge(y = -0.15)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = COND_COLS, guide = "none") + scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = gsub("\\|", "  ", k), x = "Effect size (beta)", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
                                          axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))
}
p <- (ex_plot(ex1, sprintf("Shared (significant in %d of %d)", sum(lfA[ex1, ] < 0.05), length(condsA))) | ex_plot(ex2, "Noisy estimate (galactose)") |
      ex_plot(ex3, "Fluconazole_8ug-specific")) +
  plot_annotation(caption = "Coloured: raw GWAS estimate +/- 1.96 SE.  Black: mashr estimate +/- 1.96 posterior SD.")
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_shrinkage_examples", 15, 5.5)
```

## 9.4 Numbers for the text: confirmed and not-confirmed strong-set leads

Strong set = one lead eQTL per gene (lowest P across the six datasets), without the eQTLs that have
no local / distant call (Section 4). *Confirmed* = lfsr < 0.05 in at least one dataset. Fold below
threshold = permutation threshold / lead P in the dataset where the lead has its lowest P. Datasets
with an eQTL = datasets in which the gene has any significant eQTL (any variant).

```{r text-numbers}
fT <- fits$A_main; lfT <- get_lfsr(fT$m_strong); pmT <- get_pm(fT$m_strong)
relT <- t(apply(pmT, 1, function(x) x / x[which.max(abs(x))]))
condsT <- fT$conds
lead_fold <- bind_rows(signif[condsT]) %>% group_by(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type) %>%
  slice_min(P, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>% transmute(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, fold = thr / P)
gene_ds <- bind_rows(lapply(condsT, function(cn) tibble(Gene = unique(signif[[cn]]$Gene), dataset = cn))) %>%
  count(Gene, name = "n_datasets_with_eQTL")
txt <- tibble(eQTL = rownames(pmT), confirmed = rowSums(lfT < 0.05) > 0,
              n_sign = rowSums(relT > 0), n_mag = rowSums(relT >= 0.5)) %>%
  separate(eQTL, c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(lead_fold, by = c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type")) %>%
  left_join(gene_ds, by = "Gene")
cf <- txt %>% filter(confirmed); nc <- txt %>% filter(!confirmed)
text_numbers <- tibble(
  quantity = c("strong-set leads (one per gene)", "dropped: no local / distant call",
               "confirmed (lfsr < 0.05 in >= 1 dataset)", "not confirmed",
               "median fold below threshold, not confirmed", "median fold below threshold, confirmed",
               "not-confirmed genes with an eQTL in >= 2 datasets (%)",
               "confirmed, same sign in all 6 (n)", "confirmed, same sign in all 6 (%)",
               "confirmed, sign specific to one dataset (n)",
               "confirmed, shared by magnitude in all 6 (n)", "confirmed, shared by magnitude in all 6 (%)"),
  value = c(nrow(txt), fT$n_dropped_no_call, nrow(cf), nrow(nc),
            median(nc$fold, na.rm = TRUE), median(cf$fold, na.rm = TRUE),
            100 * mean(nc$n_datasets_with_eQTL >= 2, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(cf$n_sign == length(condsT)), 100 * mean(cf$n_sign == length(condsT)),
            sum(cf$n_sign == 1),
            sum(cf$n_mag == length(condsT)), 100 * mean(cf$n_mag == length(condsT))))
knitr::kable(text_numbers, digits = 1, caption = "Numbers for the Results text (run A)")
write.csv(text_numbers, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "text_numbers_strong_set.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 9.5 Number of conditions in which eQTLs are shared

For every eQTL significant (lfsr < 0.05) in at least one condition, the number of conditions in which
its effect is shared with the condition where it is strongest: **by sign** (same sign) and **by
magnitude** (same sign and at least half as large), as in Urbut et al. (2019), Fig. 4, in all six
conditions (run A).

```{r fig-sharing-hist, fig.width = 13, fig.height = 8}
share_counts <- function(f, label) {
  pm <- get_pm(f$m_strong); lf <- get_lfsr(f$m_strong)
  pm <- pm[rowSums(lf < 0.05) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  rel <- t(apply(pm, 1, function(x) x / x[which.max(abs(x))]))
  bind_rows(tibble(set = label, definition = "Shared by sign", n = rowSums(rel > 0)),
            tibble(set = label, definition = "Shared by magnitude (within 2-fold)", n = rowSums(rel >= 0.5)))
}
hs <- bind_rows(share_counts(fits$A_main, sprintf("All conditions (run A, %d eQTLs)", sum(rowSums(get_lfsr(fits$A_main$m_strong) < 0.05) > 0)))) %>%
                # share_counts(fits$C_YPD_flu, sprintf("YPD + fluconazole (run C, %d eQTLs)", ...)): run C not reported
  mutate(definition = factor(definition, c("Shared by sign", "Shared by magnitude (within 2-fold)")))
p <- ggplot(hs, aes(n)) + geom_bar(fill = "#2C7FB8", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = after_stat(count)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.3) +
  facet_grid(definition ~ set, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:6) + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Number of conditions in which each eQTL is shared", x = "Number of conditions", y = "Number of eQTLs") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_n_conditions_shared", 13, 8)
write.csv(hs %>% count(set, definition, n_conditions = n), file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "n_conditions_shared.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-n-significant, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
ns <- bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(r) tibble(run = RUN_LABELS[[r]], n = rowSums(get_lfsr(fits[[r]]$m_strong) < 0.05))))
p <- ggplot(ns, aes(n)) + geom_bar(fill = "grey60", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
```

# 10. Are the shared eQTLs local or distant?

Every strong-set eQTL significant in at least one condition (run A) gets the local / distant call
of its lead variant from the per-condition annotation tables (`*_annotated_cis_trans.txt`; local =
any variant of the clump within 25 kb of the gene, see `README_CURRENT_FILES.md`). A lead variant
is matched to a clump whether it is the clump lead or a clump member, in any of the six datasets;
the call is a property of the variant and gene positions, so it is the same in every dataset.
eQTLs whose lead is a CNV past an S288C chromosome end (non-S288C "YX" genes) have no position and
therefore no call; they were dropped from the strong-set results right after fitting (Section 4),
so every count in this report excludes them.

Sharing groups:

- *Significantly shared in all 6*: lfsr < 0.05 in all six datasets **and** shared by magnitude in
  all six (strictest);
- *Shared by magnitude in all 6* (as in 9.5), whatever the lfsr;
- *Shared by magnitude in 2-5*;
- *Strongest dataset only*: not shared by magnitude with any other dataset.

The background is all clumped eQTLs of each dataset. The strong set keeps one lead variant per
gene (the lowest p-value), which favours each gene's strongest signal, so compare the sharing
groups with each other rather than with the background.

```{r local-distant}
# annotation tables and local / distant calls (ANNOT_DIRS, annot, ld_calls) are read in Section 4

pmA <- get_pm(fA$m_strong); lfA <- get_lfsr(fA$m_strong)
keep <- rowSums(lfA < 0.05) > 0
relA <- t(apply(pmA[keep, , drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) x / x[which.max(abs(x))]))
SHARE_LEVELS <- c("significantly shared in all 6", "shared by magnitude in all 6",
                  "shared by magnitude in 2-5", "strongest dataset only")
mash_ld <- tibble(eQTL = rownames(pmA)[keep], n_sig = rowSums(lfA[keep, , drop = FALSE] < 0.05),
                  n_mag = rowSums(relA >= 0.5), n_sign = rowSums(relA > 0)) %>%
  separate(eQTL, c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(ld_calls, by = c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type")) %>%
  mutate(sharing = factor(case_when(n_mag == ncol(pmA) & n_sig == ncol(pmA) ~ SHARE_LEVELS[1],
                                    n_mag == ncol(pmA) ~ SHARE_LEVELS[2],
                                    n_mag > 1 ~ SHARE_LEVELS[3],
                                    TRUE ~ SHARE_LEVELS[4]), SHARE_LEVELS),
         Variant_Type = factor(Variant_Type, names(ANNOT_FILES)))
cat(sprintf("%d significant eQTLs, %d without a local / distant call\n", nrow(mash_ld), sum(is.na(mash_ld$local_distant))))

ld_count <- function(d) d %>% summarise(n = n(), local = sum(local_distant == "Local", na.rm = TRUE),
                                        distant = sum(local_distant == "Distant", na.rm = TRUE),
                                        pct_local = 100 * local / (local + distant), .groups = "drop")
ld_by_sharing <- bind_rows(mash_ld %>% ld_count() %>% mutate(sharing = "all significant eQTLs"),
                           mash_ld %>% group_by(sharing) %>% ld_count() %>% mutate(sharing = as.character(sharing))) %>%
  relocate(sharing)
knitr::kable(ld_by_sharing, digits = 1, caption = "Local vs distant mashr eQTLs by sharing (run A)")

# is each sharing group more often local than all other significant eQTLs?
ld_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(SHARE_LEVELS[1:2], function(s) {
  d <- mash_ld %>% filter(!is.na(local_distant))
  in_s <- if (s == SHARE_LEVELS[2]) d$n_mag == ncol(pmA) else d$sharing == s   # "by magnitude in all 6" includes the strict group
  ft <- fisher.test(table(factor(in_s, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$local_distant == "Local", c(TRUE, FALSE))))
  tibble(group = s, n_group = sum(in_s), pct_local_group = 100 * mean(d$local_distant[in_s] == "Local"),
         pct_local_rest = 100 * mean(d$local_distant[!in_s] == "Local"),
         fisher_OR = unname(ft$estimate), fisher_p = ft$p.value)
}))
knitr::kable(ld_tests %>% mutate(fisher_p = format(fisher_p, digits = 2)), digits = 2,
             caption = "Shared eQTLs vs all other significant eQTLs: % local (Fisher's exact test)")

# the other direction: given that an eQTL is local (or distant), how likely is it to be shared?
# Local effects are usually larger, and a larger effect is easier to call significant in all six
# datasets, so the logistic regression also adjusts for the eQTL's strongest effect
# (max |posterior mean / posterior SD| over the six datasets).
psdA <- get_psd(fA$m_strong)
mash_ld <- mash_ld %>%
  mutate(max_abs_z = apply(abs(pmA[keep, , drop = FALSE] / psdA[keep, , drop = FALSE]), 1, max),
         sig_shared_all6 = sharing == SHARE_LEVELS[1],
         mag_shared_all6 = n_mag == ncol(pmA))

p_shared <- mash_ld %>% filter(!is.na(local_distant)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sig_shared_all6, mag_shared_all6), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "shared") %>%
  mutate(outcome = recode(outcome, sig_shared_all6 = "significantly shared in all 6",
                          mag_shared_all6 = "shared by magnitude in all 6")) %>%
  group_by(outcome, local_distant) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), n_shared = sum(shared), pct_shared = 100 * mean(shared),
            median_max_abs_z = median(max_abs_z), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(p_shared, digits = 1, caption = "P(shared | local) vs P(shared | distant)")

shared_given_ld <- bind_rows(lapply(c("sig_shared_all6", "mag_shared_all6"), function(y) {
  d <- mash_ld %>% filter(!is.na(local_distant)) %>% mutate(local = local_distant == "Local", shared = .data[[y]])
  a <- sum(d$shared & d$local); n1 <- sum(d$local); b <- sum(d$shared & !d$local); n0 <- sum(!d$local)
  log_rr <- log((a / n1) / (b / n0)); se <- sqrt(1 / a - 1 / n1 + 1 / b - 1 / n0)
  fit <- summary(glm(shared ~ local + log(max_abs_z), family = binomial, data = d))$coefficients
  tibble(outcome = y, pct_shared_local = 100 * a / n1, pct_shared_distant = 100 * b / n0,
         relative_risk = exp(log_rr), rr_ci_low = exp(log_rr - 1.96 * se), rr_ci_high = exp(log_rr + 1.96 * se),
         fisher_p = fisher.test(table(d$local, d$shared))$p.value,
         adj_OR_local = exp(fit["localTRUE", "Estimate"]), adj_p_local = fit["localTRUE", "Pr(>|z|)"])
}))
knitr::kable(shared_given_ld %>% mutate(across(c(fisher_p, adj_p_local), ~ format(.x, digits = 2))), digits = 2,
             caption = "How much more likely a local eQTL is to be shared than a distant one. adj_OR_local: logistic regression adjusted for log max |z|")
write.csv(shared_given_ld, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_shared_given_local_distant.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

ld_by_type <- mash_ld %>% group_by(sharing, Variant_Type) %>% ld_count()
knitr::kable(ld_by_type %>% select(sharing, Variant_Type, n, pct_local) %>%
               pivot_wider(names_from = Variant_Type, values_from = c(n, pct_local)),
             digits = 1, caption = "Number of eQTLs and % local per sharing group and variant type")

ld_background <- annot %>% group_by(dataset) %>% ld_count()
knitr::kable(ld_background, digits = 1, caption = "Background: all clumped eQTLs per dataset")

write.csv(mash_ld, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_eQTLs_local_distant_A_main.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bind_rows(ld_by_sharing %>% mutate(table = "by sharing"),
                    ld_by_type %>% mutate(sharing = as.character(sharing), table = "by sharing and variant type"),
                    ld_background %>% rename(sharing = dataset) %>% mutate(table = "background, all clumped eQTLs")),
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_local_distant_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ld_tests, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_local_distant_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 10.1 Why mashr has fewer local eQTLs than each dataset

Each dataset's annotation tables count every clump (a gene can have several local and distant
clumps). The mashr strong set keeps **one variant per gene**: the lowest p-value across all six
datasets and variant types. A gene with a local eQTL is therefore represented by a distant variant
whenever one of its distant eQTLs has a lower p-value in any dataset, and it drops out of the
results when its lead is not significant (lfsr < 0.05) in any dataset after shrinkage. The table
follows the YPD.1 and YPD.2 local eQTLs through these steps.

```{r local-trace}
strong_genes <- unique(sub("\\|.*", "", rownames(pmA)))
local_trace <- bind_rows(lapply(c("YPD.1", "YPD.2"), function(ds) {
  a <- annot %>% filter(dataset == ds)
  g <- unique(a$Pheno[a$local_distant %in% "Local"])
  m <- mash_ld %>% filter(Gene %in% g)
  tibble(dataset = ds,
         local_clumps = sum(a$local_distant %in% "Local"),
         genes_with_local_eQTL = length(g),
         of_which_also_distant_eQTL = sum(g %in% a$Pheno[a$local_distant %in% "Distant"]),
         genes_in_mashr_strong_set = sum(g %in% strong_genes),
         lead_significant_in_mashr = nrow(m),
         lead_is_local = sum(m$local_distant %in% "Local"),
         lead_is_distant = sum(m$local_distant %in% "Distant"),
         local_lead_significantly_shared_all6 = sum(m$local_distant %in% "Local" & m$sharing == SHARE_LEVELS[1]))
}))
knitr::kable(local_trace, caption = "Local eQTLs of each YPD replicate, followed into the mashr results (one lead variant per gene)")
write.csv(local_trace, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_local_eQTL_trace_YPD.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

How the distant (left) and local (right) mashr eQTLs are shared. Every bar is a count out of all
significant eQTLs of that location (top bar); the label gives the count and % of that total.

- *Shared by sign in all 6*: same sign as in the strongest dataset in all six datasets
- *Shared by magnitude in all 6*: same sign and at least half the strongest effect in all six (includes the next bar)
- *Significant and shared by magnitude in all 6*: also lfsr < 0.05 in all six (strictest)
- *Shared by magnitude in 2-5*: shared by magnitude with 1-4 other datasets
- *Not shared with any other dataset*: significant, but shared by magnitude with no other dataset
  (previously "strongest dataset only")

The first three bars are nested; the last three plus "shared by magnitude in all 6" add up to the total.

```{r fig-local-distant, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 5.5}
LD_COLS <- c(Local = "#eb6834", Distant = "#2a78d6")
SHARE_STEPS <- c("All significant eQTLs", "Shared by sign in all 6", "Shared by magnitude in all 6",
                 "Significant and shared by magnitude in all 6", "Shared by magnitude in 2-5",
                 "Not shared with any other dataset")
ld_steps <- mash_ld %>% filter(!is.na(local_distant)) %>% group_by(local_distant) %>%
  summarise(`All significant eQTLs` = n(),
            `Shared by sign in all 6` = sum(n_sign == ncol(pmA)),
            `Shared by magnitude in all 6` = sum(n_mag == ncol(pmA)),
            `Significant and shared by magnitude in all 6` = sum(sharing == SHARE_LEVELS[1]),
            `Shared by magnitude in 2-5` = sum(sharing == SHARE_LEVELS[3]),
            `Not shared with any other dataset` = sum(sharing == SHARE_LEVELS[4]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-local_distant, names_to = "category", values_to = "n") %>%
  group_by(local_distant) %>% mutate(pct = 100 * n / n[category == "All significant eQTLs"]) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(category = factor(category, rev(SHARE_STEPS)))
knitr::kable(ld_steps %>% pivot_wider(names_from = local_distant, values_from = c(n, pct)), digits = 1,
             caption = "Sharing of distant and local mashr eQTLs")
write.csv(ld_steps, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "mash_local_distant_sharing_breakdown.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

ld_side <- function(loc) {
  d <- ld_steps %>% filter(local_distant == loc) %>% mutate(total = category == "All significant eQTLs")
  ggplot(d, aes(n, category, fill = total)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.65, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(total, sprintf("%d", n), sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, pct))),
              hjust = -0.1, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "grey70", "FALSE" = LD_COLS[[loc]]), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
    labs(title = sprintf("%s eQTLs (n = %s)", loc, format(max(d$n), big.mark = ",")), x = "Number of eQTLs", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "black"), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
}
p_dist <- ld_side("Distant"); p_loc <- ld_side("Local")
p <- p_dist + (p_loc + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank()))
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_local_distant_by_sharing", 14, 5.5)
save_fig(p_dist, "Fig_mash_local_distant_by_sharing_distant", 9, 5.5)
save_fig(p_loc, "Fig_mash_local_distant_by_sharing_local", 9, 5.5)
```

## 10.2 Publication figure: local vs distant eQTLs and sharing by magnitude

(a) Composition of the shared list: local and distant eQTLs among the eQTLs shared by magnitude
in all six datasets. (b) Yet a local eQTL
is more likely to be shared by magnitude in all six datasets than a distant one (95% Wilson CI;
odds ratio from the logistic regression adjusted for effect strength, Section 10). (c) The same
comparison within bins of effect strength (max |posterior mean / posterior SD| over the six
datasets): local eQTLs are more often shared at matched strength, so the difference is not only
because local effects are larger. Numbers = eQTLs per bar / point.

```{r fig-local-distant-pub, fig.width = 25.5, fig.height = 8}
LD_PUB <- c(Local = "#eb6834", Distant = "#2a78d6")            # local / distant, same in every panel
LD_TINT <- c(Local = "#f6b9a0", Distant = "#a9c9ef")           # not shared: tint of the same hue
# same bold publication theme as the other Figure 4 panels, with light grid lines
theme_pub <- pub_theme + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
                               plot.caption = element_text(face = "bold", size = PUB_SMALL - 2, colour = "grey30"))

ldp <- mash_ld %>% filter(!is.na(local_distant)) %>%
  mutate(local_distant = factor(local_distant, c("Local", "Distant")))
wilson <- function(x, n) { ci <- prop.test(x, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int; tibble(lo = 100 * ci[1], hi = 100 * ci[2]) }

# (a) composition of the shared list: local and distant eQTLs among those shared by magnitude in all six
pa_dat <- ldp %>% filter(mag_shared_all6) %>% count(local_distant) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
pa <- ggplot(pa_dat, aes(n, local_distant, fill = local_distant)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, pct)), hjust = -0.1, size = PUB_LABEL, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LD_PUB, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(title = "a  Shared eQTLs: local vs distant", x = "eQTLs shared by magnitude in all 6", y = NULL) +
  theme_pub + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3))

# (b) % shared by magnitude in all six, with 95% CI
pb_dat <- ldp %>% group_by(local_distant) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), x = sum(mag_shared_all6), pct = 100 * x / n, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci = map2(x, n, wilson)) %>% unnest(ci)
st <- shared_given_ld %>% filter(outcome == "mag_shared_all6")
pb <- ggplot(pb_dat, aes(local_distant, pct, fill = local_distant)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = sprintf("%.0f%%\n(%d / %d)", pct, x, n)), vjust = -0.25, size = PUB_LABEL, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 118, size = PUB_LABEL - 0.5, fontface = "bold",
           label = sprintf("adjusted OR = %.1f, p = %s", st$adj_OR_local, format(st$adj_p_local, digits = 1))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LD_PUB, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 122), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(title = "b  Local eQTLs are more often shared", x = NULL, y = "% shared by magnitude\nin all 6 datasets") +
  theme_pub

# (c) the same within bins of effect strength
Z_BREAKS <- c(0, 3, 4, 5, Inf); Z_LABELS <- c("< 3", "3-4", "4-5", "> 5")
pc_dat <- ldp %>% mutate(z_bin = cut(max_abs_z, Z_BREAKS, labels = Z_LABELS)) %>%
  group_by(z_bin, local_distant) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), x = sum(mag_shared_all6), pct = 100 * x / n, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci = map2(x, n, wilson)) %>% unnest(ci)
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.5)
pc <- ggplot(pc_dat, aes(z_bin, pct, colour = local_distant, group = local_distant)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.5, position = dodge) +
  geom_point(size = 5, position = dodge) +
  geom_text(aes(y = -4, label = n), position = dodge, size = PUB_LABEL - 1, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey30", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = LD_PUB, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-8, 102), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  labs(title = "c  ... at the same effect strength", x = "effect strength (max |z| across datasets)",
       y = "% shared by magnitude\nin all 6 datasets", caption = "numbers: eQTLs per point") +
  theme_pub + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# (a, alternative) all significant eQTLs, local and distant, split into shared by magnitude in all 6 and not
pa2_dat <- ldp %>% count(local_distant, mag_shared_all6) %>%
  mutate(fill_key = paste(local_distant, mag_shared_all6))
pa2_tot <- pa2_dat %>% group_by(local_distant) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), shared = sum(n[mag_shared_all6]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("%d shared + %d not (n = %d)", shared, total - shared, total))
pa2 <- ggplot(pa2_dat, aes(n, local_distant, fill = fill_key)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(data = pa2_tot, aes(total, local_distant, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.05, size = PUB_LABEL, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Local TRUE" = LD_PUB[["Local"]], "Local FALSE" = LD_TINT[["Local"]],
                               "Distant TRUE" = LD_PUB[["Distant"]], "Distant FALSE" = LD_TINT[["Distant"]]),
                    breaks = c("Distant TRUE", "Distant FALSE", "Local TRUE", "Local FALSE"),
                    labels = c("distant, shared by magnitude in all 6", "distant, not shared in all 6",
                               "local, shared by magnitude in all 6", "local, not shared in all 6")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.6))) +
  labs(title = "a  Local and distant eQTLs", x = "mashr eQTLs", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_pub + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical",
                    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3))

# combined figure in two versions (panel a = shared list only, or split), and each panel on its own
p <- pa + pb + pc + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.2))
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_sharing", 3 * PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
p <- pa2 + pb + pc + plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 0.8, 1.2))
print(p); save_fig(p, "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_sharing_split", 3.3 * PANEL_W, PANEL_H + 1)
# individual panels: same plots without the a / b / c letters in the titles
untag <- function(p, title) p + labs(title = title)
save_fig(untag(pa,  "Shared eQTLs: local vs distant"),                 "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_panel_a_shared_only", PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
save_fig(untag(pa2, "Local and distant eQTLs"),                        "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_panel_a_split", PANEL_W, PANEL_H + 1)
save_fig(untag(pb,  "Local eQTLs are more often shared"),              "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_panel_b", PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
save_fig(untag(pc,  "Local eQTLs are more often shared\nat the same effect strength"), "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_panel_c", PANEL_W, PANEL_H)
write.csv(bind_rows(pa_dat %>% mutate(panel = "a"),
                    pa2_dat %>% select(-fill_key) %>% mutate(panel = "a_split"),
                    pb_dat %>% mutate(panel = "b"),
                    pc_dat %>% mutate(panel = "c", z_bin = as.character(z_bin))),
          file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_mash_pub_local_vs_distant_sharing_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
